summary: On-chain multi-chain ERC-20 risk assessment. Validators agree on a 29-ordinal feature vector; every score is arithmetic over it.
note: Studionet and Bradbury run the same artifacts. Verify with: shasum -a 256 build/*.min.py and compare against the sha256 fields below, or genlayer code <address> | diff - build/TokenScope.min.py

TokenScope.fee_note: fee_wei set to 0 on this demo deployment. The genlayer CLI hardcodes value: 0n on writes, so there is no way to attach payable value from the command line; the fee path is exercised in the offline suite instead. DEFAULT_FEE_WEI is 0.01 GEN in the source.

render_probe.why: throwaway diagnostic, not part of TokenScope; the evidence behind docs/PROBE.md, including the 422 on ?type=ERC-20 and the transient 500 from base.blockscout.com

TokenScope.fee_note: fee_wei set to 0, same reason as Studionet.

size_finding.claim: AuditCourt's notes put the GenVM runner deploy limit at 48 KB.
size_finding.measured: That is stale. The 50,199-byte TokenScope artifact deployed successfully to BOTH Studionet and Bradbury.
size_finding.why_it_matters: Several hours of size optimisation were being spent against an unverified constant; deploying the oversized artifact answered it in one transaction.

cross_network_result.note: Byte-identical content_hash and score produced on Studionet and on Bradbury by different validator sets, from the same artifact. The vector, not the network, decides the score.

composability_result.consumer: RiskConsumer.list_token goes through TokenScope.require_safe, which REVERTS rather than returning false.
composability_result.listed: USDT on Bradbury: tier blue_chip, overall 86, rug_level MEDIUM, trade_cap 10000000
composability_result.revert_proof: list_token on an unscored token returns [EXPECTED] no score for ethereum:0x514910771af9ca656af840dff83e8264ecf986ca, while preview_listing on the same token degrades to {listable:false, reason:'never scored', badge:'UNSCORED'}
